title: Reformed confessions affirm infused renovation
source_text: IV. Igitur communi consensu Theologi Reformati & Orthodoxi docent, Deum fideles, quos in gratiam recipit, intus renovare & sanctificare, illisque novam ju-stitiam & sanctitatem infundere, qua Dei creatoris & Redemptoris sui imaginem re-ferant. Qua de re privatorum sententias congerere superfluum foret, & infinitae operae. Sed tamen, ut clarius & certius appareat quam pudenda sit ista calumnia, visum est quaedam proferre publicis Ecclesiarum Reformatorum Confessionibus testata atque ex-posita. Sic ergo habet Confessio Reformatorum ex Polonia publice in Conventu Thoruniensi lecta Ann. 1645. cap. 4. sect. 2. num. 7. Falso accusamur quasi omnem inhaerentem justitiam fidelibus negemus, eosque sola externa justitiae Christi impu-tatione, quae sit sine ulla interna renovatione, justificari statuamus: cum tamen solis poenitentibus, & viva fide in Christum credentibus justitiam imputari, simulque per eandem fidem a Spiritu Sancto corda contrita vivificari, ad ardentem erga Christum charitatem & novae obedientiae studium excitari, a pravis videlicet cupiditatibus mun-dari, atque ita justitiam & sanctitatem vitae novae inchoari, & in dies perfici doceamus. Quibus consona tradit Anglicana Confessio eodem anno publicata, cap. 13. de Sanctificatione, ubi docet illos qui sunt efficaciter vocati realiter & personaliter magis ac magis sanctificari virtute mortis & resurrectionis Christi, totius corporis peccati dominium in ipsis prosterni, eosque magis ac magis in omni salutari gratia roborari, ut studeant verae sanctitati, sine qua nemo videbit Dominum. Similiter Gallica Refor-matorum Confessio, articulo 22. diserte asserit nos per fidem in vitae novitatem rege-nerari, & per eandem fidem accipere gratiam sancte vivendi, & in timore Dei, cum per naturam servi peccati simus.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore by common consent Reformed and Orthodox theologians teach that God inwardly renews and sanctifies the faithful whom he receives into grace, and infuses into them a new righteousness and holiness by which they bear the image of God their Creator and Redeemer. To heap up private opinions on this would be superfluous and endless labor. Yet, that it may appear more clearly and surely how shameful that calumny is, it has seemed good to bring forward certain things attested and set forth in the public Confessions of the Reformed Churches. Thus the Confession of the Reformed from Poland, publicly read in the Convention of Thorn in the year 1645, chapter 4, section 2, number 7: We are falsely accused as if we denied all inherent righteousness to believers, and as if we held that they are justified by the mere external imputation of Christ's righteousness without any internal renovation: whereas we teach that righteousness is imputed only to the penitent and to those who believe in Christ with a living faith, and that at the same time by the same faith contrite hearts are vivified by the Holy Spirit, stirred to ardent charity toward Christ and to zeal for new obedience, cleansed from wicked desires, and thus that the righteousness and holiness of the new life is begun and perfected day by day. Concordant with this is the Anglican Confession published the same year, chapter 13 on Sanctification, which teaches that those who are effectually called are really and personally more and more sanctified by the virtue of Christ's death and resurrection, that the dominion of the whole body of sin is overthrown in them, and that they are more and more strengthened in every saving grace so as to pursue true holiness, without which no one will see the Lord. Likewise the French Confession of the Reformed, article 22, expressly asserts that we are regenerated by faith into newness of life, and by the same faith receive grace to live holily and in the fear of God, although by nature we are slaves of sin.
pass_b_english: Reformed consensus: God inwardly renews and sanctifies those he receives, infusing new justice imaging Creator and Redeemer.
Polish 1645, Anglican sanctification article, and French Confession all teach living faith with inward vivification and growth in holiness.
